verdict.line: You lose extended trades before level 6 if you sit in his Q line or let him stack to 2, but you win the matchup overall (54.9% over 616 games) once Black Cleaver and Death's Dance let your burst punch through his shields and his All Out healing.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes, range 450) out-ranges every tool in your kit (Q 275, W 260, E 250), and his E (Footwork) shield lets him no-trade you while he stacks toward the level-6 wall combo on R (All Out). You can't win the laning phase on mechanics alone — you win it on the clock, surviving the poke until Black Cleaver and Death's Dance let your Q-W burst outvalue his shields and sustain.

theirWindow.when: When K'Sante reaches 2 Ntofo Strikes stacks
theirWindow.what: His second Q stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in for a follow-up trade he's favored to win. Don't give him a clean second hit — step outside his 450-range line rather than farming through it, since his E (Footwork) shield still covers whatever comes after the pull.

yourWindow.what: With no shield or dash available, commit fully: Q (Broken Wings) in, W (Ki Burst) to stun, then dump remaining Q charges and weave autos. He has no Footwork cooldown to escape or cushion the burst.

start.why: 94.9% pick rate and 55.4% win rate over 650 games — the extra sustain and early AD matter when you can't freely trade into his Q poke.

boots.why: 56.5% win rate over 398 games; the ability haste shortens your Q (Broken Wings) and W (Ki Burst) loops so you can punish the windows when his Footwork (E) is down.

core.why: Shreds the armor he's stacking as a tank bruiser, directly closing the gap that makes him favored early.
Converts his burst damage into delayed, mitigated damage — exactly what you need surviving his R (All Out) engage near walls.
The anti-heal cuts into the bonus healing his R grants while All Out, so he can't stabilize off his ultimate.

situational.when: you're ahead in lane and want an earlier burst-and-shield spike to force all-ins before his items come online
you need the extra ability haste to loop Q (Broken Wings) and R (Blade of the Exile) faster in extended skirmishes
the enemy team adds heavy magic damage alongside K'Sante and you need the shield and magic resist instead

runes.keystoneWhy: Riven's Q-W-auto loop stacks Conqueror fast in extended trades, and the healing scales to offset the chip damage you take from his Q poke while you wait for item power.

summoners.why: 94.2% pick rate at 56.7% win rate — Ignite punishes the all-in windows when his Footwork (E) is on cooldown and denies the sustain his R (All Out) healing would otherwise give back.

playing.title: Deny the second Q stack
playing.detail: Don't stand in his Ntofo Strikes line twice in a row before level 6 — the second stack fires a shockwave that pulls you into a trade he wins.

playing.title: Punish Footwork cooldown
playing.detail: Track every time he uses E (Footwork) to shield or reposition. The moment it's down, your Q-W all-in connects without him having an escape or damage cushion.

playing.title: Save E for his W charge-up
playing.detail: Path Maker telegraphs with a visible channel before the dash. Step outside its 600 range rather than tanking it — Valor only blocks damage, it doesn't stop the knockback or stun.

playing.title: Respect walls after level 6
playing.detail: His R (All Out) knocks you through the nearest wall, then he dashes in empowered with reduced defenses but more damage and healing. Don't fight low near lane walls.

playing.title: Weave autos into your combo
playing.detail: Runic Blade only pays off on basic attacks — don't burn every Q charge without an auto in between or you're wasting blade stacks.

playing.title: Farm the lane, win the game
playing.detail: You're not favored to win most all-ins before 6. Play for CS and wave state, then let Black Cleaver and Death's Dance flip the matchup around level 9-12.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells come straight from measured Riven vs K'Sante games on the current patch (616 games, 54.9% win rate). The tactical reasoning — trade timing, cooldown tells, and the power-curve calls — is my own read of the ability kits, not sourced from the stats.
